questions.stem: What is a force?

explain.why: Sound is not a force. A force is a push or a pull.
Light lets us see. A force is not light.
Heat is energy that makes things hot. A force is not heat.

solution: A force is a push or a pull on an object.

questions.stem: Which of these is a push?
options: Dragging a bag along the floor
Opening a drawer by its handle
Pulling a rope in a tug-of-war

explain.why: Dragging uses a pull on the bag.
You pull the drawer towards you.
Pulling a rope is a pull.

solution: Pressing a doorbell pushes the button away from you. The others are pulls.

questions.stem: Which of these is a pull?
options: Pressing a switch on the wall
Opening a drawer by its handle

explain.why: A hammer pushes the nail into the wood.
Pressing a switch is a push.
A kick is a push on the ball.

solution: You pull the handle towards you to open a drawer.

questions.stem: Ali kicks a football that is lying still on the grass. What does the force of his kick do to the ball?
options: It makes the ball change its shape for ever
It makes the ball slow down
It makes the ball start to move

explain.why: The ball may squash a little but goes back to its shape.
The ball was not moving, so it cannot be stopped.
The ball was still. A force from the kick moves it.

solution: A force can make a still object start to move.

questions.stem: A goalkeeper catches a fast-moving ball. What does the force from the goalkeeper's hands do to the ball?
options: It makes the ball change direction
It makes the ball speed up
It makes the ball stop moving
It makes the ball start moving

explain.why: The goalkeeper holds the ball, so it does not go in a new direction.
The hands make the ball stop, not move faster.
The ball was already moving.

solution: A force can stop a moving object. The hands stop the ball.

questions.stem: A batsman hits a ball coming towards him and the ball flies back the other way. What effect does the bat's force have?
options: It makes the ball stay still
It changes the shape of the ball for ever
It changes the direction of the ball

explain.why: The ball is still moving after it is hit.
The ball goes back to its shape afterwards.
A force does not change how heavy the ball is.

solution: The ball was moving towards the batsman and now moves away. The bat changed its direction.

questions.stem: A cyclist pedals harder on a flat road. What happens to the bicycle?

explain.why: A bicycle does not change shape when you pedal harder.
A bigger force from the pedals speeds the bicycle up.
Pedalling harder is a bigger push, so the bicycle does not stop.

solution: A bigger push makes a moving bicycle go faster.

questions.stem: Mei squeezes a soft sponge in her hand. What does her force do to the sponge?
options: It makes the sponge move up
It makes the sponge stop moving
It changes the shape of the sponge
It makes the sponge speed up

explain.why: The sponge stays in her hand. It gets squashed.
The sponge was not moving.
The sponge is not moving. It is being squashed.

solution: Squeezing is a force that changes the shape of an object.

questions.stem: A cyclist presses the brakes while riding. What happens to the bicycle?

explain.why: Brakes do not turn the bicycle.
The brakes slow it down. It keeps moving forwards until it stops.
Brakes make a bicycle go slower.

solution: A force from the brakes slows down a moving object.

questions.stem: Which force pulls objects towards the ground?

explain.why: Elastic spring force acts when a spring or rubber band is stretched.
A magnetic force pulls on iron, not on everything.
Friction acts between surfaces that touch.

solution: Gravity pulls everything towards the Earth.

questions.stem: A magnet pulls an iron nail towards it without touching it. Which force is this?

explain.why: The nail moves sideways or up, not down.
Friction needs two surfaces to rub together.
No spring or rubber band is being stretched.

solution: A magnet attracts iron with magnetic force, even from a short distance.

questions.stem: A box slides along the floor and stops after a while. Which force slows it down?

explain.why: Gravity pulls the box down, not backwards.
There is no stretched spring.
The floor is not a magnet.

solution: Friction between the box and the floor slows the box.

questions.stem: A rubber band is stretched and then let go. It springs back to its first length. Which force makes it spring back?

explain.why: Gravity pulls the band down, not back along its length.
A rubber band is not a magnet.
Friction needs rubbing surfaces.

solution: A stretched rubber band pulls back because of elastic spring force.

questions.stem: Which of these forces can act on an object without touching it?

explain.why: A hand has to touch the object to push it.
Friction acts only when two surfaces touch.
A rope must be tied to the object.

solution: Magnetic force and gravity act from a distance. The others need contact.

questions.stem: A ripe mango falls from a tree to the ground. Which force pulls it down?

explain.why: Friction acts against sliding, not falling.
There is no spring in a falling mango.
The ground does not pull the mango like a magnet.

solution: Gravity pulls the mango to the Earth.

questions.stem: A boy pushes a heavy door shut. What does the force do to the door?
options: It changes the shape of the door for ever

explain.why: The door does not stay bent. It moves.
A force does not change how heavy something is.
A force does not change how heavy something is.

solution: The push moves the door from open to shut.

questions.stem: Which of the following shows a force changing the shape of an object?
options: Rolling a ball along the ground
Kicking a ball across a field
Catching a ball in the air
Pressing a ball of clay flat

explain.why: Rolling makes the ball move. Its shape stays the same.
A kick makes the ball move.
This stops the ball. Its shape stays the same.

solution: Pressing a ball of clay changes its shape.

questions.stem: What is the unit for measuring the size of a force?

explain.why: Gram is a unit of mass.
Centimetre measures length.
Degree Celsius measures temperature.

solution: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.stem: Nina pushes a swing in the same direction that it is already moving. What happens to the swing?

explain.why: A swing does not change shape.
A push the same way adds speed.
A push in the same direction does not stop it.

solution: A push in the direction of motion speeds up a moving object.

questions.stem: A ball rolls towards a wall and bounces back. What effect does the wall's force have on the ball?
options: It makes the ball keep going the same way
It changes the direction of the ball

explain.why: The ball does not keep going. It comes back.
The wall does not make the ball float.
Forces do not change how heavy the ball is.

solution: The wall pushes the ball back, so its direction changes.

questions.stem: A small magnet sticks to a fridge door. Which force holds it there?

explain.why: Gravity pulls the magnet down. It does not hold it on the door.
Friction would not hold it up without the magnet pulling it.
No spring is stretched or squashed.

solution: The magnet is pulled onto the iron door by magnetic force.

questions.stem: A child jumps on a trampoline and is pushed back up into the air. Which force pushes the child up?

explain.why: Gravity pulls the child down.
A trampoline is not a magnet.
Friction acts across surfaces that slide, not when you bounce.

solution: The stretched trampoline springs back and pushes the child up. This is elastic spring force.

questions.stem: Which of these forces needs the two objects to touch each other?
options: The pull of the Earth on the Moon

explain.why: A magnet can pull iron from a distance.
This is gravity, which needs no contact.
Gravity acts from a distance.

solution: Friction happens only where two surfaces touch.

questions.stem: A trolley rolls to the right across a rough floor and slows down. Which arrow shows the force that slows it?
options: None of them, since nothing is pushing it

explain.why: Friction between the wheels and the floor slows it, and that is shown by one of the arrows.
Arrow T points down. That is gravity, which does not slow the trolley.
Arrow R points the same way as the trolley moves, so it would speed it up.

solution: Friction acts against the motion, so it points left (S).

questions.stem:
Which of the following situations show a force changing the direction of a moving object?
A: A tennis ball hits a wall and bounces back.
B: A footballer stops a rolling ball with his foot.
C: A hockey stick hits a puck and turns it.
D: A girl squashes a rubber ball.

explain.why: B stops a ball and D changes the shape of a ball.
B shows a force stopping a ball, not changing its direction.
D changes shape, not direction.

solution: A and C: the force turns the moving ball or puck.
B stops an object. D changes shape.

questions.stem:
Which of the following situations show a force changing the shape of an object?
A: A boy bends a plastic ruler.
B: A girl kicks a ball.
C: A cook rolls dough flat with a rolling pin.
D: A man pulls a trolley.

explain.why: B makes a ball move, which is not a change of shape.
Both of these make something move.
D makes the trolley move.

solution: Bending a ruler and flattening dough change shape.
Kicking a ball and pulling a trolley make things move.

questions.stem:
Which of the following forces act on an object without touching it?
A: Friction.
B: Gravitational force.
C: Magnetic force.
D: Elastic spring force.

explain.why: Both friction and a stretched spring need contact.
A spring needs contact to push or pull.
Friction needs the surfaces to touch.

solution: Gravity and magnetic forces can act across a gap.
Friction and a spring's force need contact.

questions.stem: The table shows what happens to four objects when a force acts on each. In which situation does the force make the object speed up?

explain.why: R slows the object down.
P stops the object.
Q changes the shape of the object.

solution: A car that begins to go faster is speeding up.
That is situation S.

questions.stem: The table shows what happens to four objects. In which situation does the force change the direction of a moving object?

explain.why: S changes the shape of a spring.
Q makes a still object start moving.
P makes the object go faster.

solution: A ball that goes the other way after hitting a wall has its direction changed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a contact force?
options: The force of a ball bouncing off a hard floor
The pull of the Earth on a falling stone
The pull of the Earth on the Moon
The pull of a magnet on a paper clip held a little way off

explain.why: Gravity acts without touching.
Gravity acts across space without touching.
A magnet pulls through a gap, so this does not need contact.

solution: The floor must touch the ball to push it back up.

questions.stem: A girl pushes a toy car and lets it go. It rolls along the floor and slowly comes to a stop. What stops the car?
options: The magnetic force of the floor on the car
The pull of gravity on the toy car as it rolls
Friction between the wheels and the floor
The push she gave the car at the start

explain.why: The floor is not a magnet.
Gravity pulls the car down. It does not slow it down sideways.
Her push started the car moving. It does not stop it.

solution: Friction acts against the motion, so it slows the car and finally stops it.

questions.stem: Which of these will use elastic spring force?
options: A catapult that is pulled back
A boy sliding down a playground slide
A magnet lifting a pin off a table
A ball falling from the edge of a table

explain.why: Gravity pulls him, and friction slows him.
That is a magnetic force.
That is gravity.

solution: The stretched rubber of a catapult springs back and throws the stone.

questions.stem: Mei hangs a metal spoon from a magnet. She says: 'Two forces act on the spoon.' Which are the two forces?
options: Gravitational force and elastic spring force
Frictional force and elastic spring force

explain.why: The spoon is not sliding on anything, so there is no friction.
There is no spring. The magnet holds the spoon.
Neither of these forces acts on the hanging spoon.

solution: The magnet pulls the spoon up and gravity pulls it down.

questions.stem: Ben says: 'Gravity pulls only on heavy things.' Which example shows that Ben is wrong?
options: A magnet pulls an iron nail
A heavy stone falls to the ground
A light feather also falls to the ground

explain.why: This is magnetic force, not gravity.
A heavy stone falling does not show that light things are pulled.
A floating boat does not show whether gravity pulls on light things.

solution: A feather is light, but it still falls. So gravity pulls on light things too.

questions.stem: A rubber band is stretched by a pull and gets longer. What effect does the pull have on the rubber band?
options: It makes the band speed up
It makes the band stop moving
It changes the direction of the band
It changes the shape of the band

explain.why: The band is not moving faster. It is longer.
The band was not moving.
The band does not go in a new direction.

solution: Stretching is a force that changes shape.

questions.stem: A woman pushes a heavy box along a floor. She stops pushing and the box stops after a short distance. Which force made the box stop?
options: Friction between the box and the floor
The elastic spring force of the floor
The magnetic force of the floor

explain.why: There is no spring.
Gravity pulls the box down, not backwards.
The floor does not attract the box.

solution: Friction opposes the sliding of the box. It slows it and stops it.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs lists forces that both need contact?
options: Friction and a push by a hand
Magnetic force and a pull by a rope

explain.why: Gravity needs no contact.
Neither of them needs contact.
A magnet needs no contact.

solution: Friction and a push by a hand act only when things touch.

questions.stem: A girl throws a ball straight up. Which effect does the force of her throw have on the ball?
options: It makes the ball stop in the air
It makes the ball change shape for ever
It makes the ball start moving up

explain.why: Gravity slows the ball later. The throw starts it moving.
The shape of the ball does not stay changed.
Falling is caused by gravity, not the throw.

solution: The throw makes a ball that was still start to move upwards.

questions.stem: A box slides to the right on the floor and slows down. Arrows P, Q and R show forces. Which statement is correct?
options: Q is friction and it slows the box
P is friction and it slows the box
Q is the push from a hand that slows the box
R is friction and it slows the box

explain.why: P points the way the box is moving, so it would not slow the box.
No hand is pushing. Q is the friction between the box and floor.
R points down. That is gravity.

solution: Friction acts against the motion, so it points to the left.
Q is friction, and it makes the box slow down.

questions.stem: A magnet hangs from a spring above an iron nail. The spring is stretched. Which forces act on the magnet?
options: Gravity, magnetic force and elastic spring force
Magnetic force and elastic spring force only
Gravity and elastic spring force only

explain.why: Gravity pulls on everything, including the magnet.
The spring is stretched and pulls on the magnet, so there is also an elastic spring force.
The nail is attracted by the magnet, so there is also a magnetic force on the magnet.

solution: Gravity pulls the magnet down.
The nail pulls it down by magnetic force.
The stretched spring pulls it up.

questions.stem: A skier travels down a slope at a high speed, then the ground flattens and she slows down and stops. Which sequence shows the effects of forces on her motion?
options: Speeds up, then stops, then slows down
Slows down, then speeds up, then stops
Stops, then speeds up, then slows down
Speeds up, then slows down, then stops

explain.why: She slows down before she stops.
She speeds up on the slope first.
She does not stop at the top.

solution: Gravity speeds her up on the slope.
Friction slows her on the flat and finally stops her.

questions.stem: Jun says that friction always makes a moving object slow down. Which situation shows friction helping to make something move?
options: A parachute falling to the ground
A box sliding to a stop

explain.why: This slows down a fall. It does not help make the person move forward.
There is very little friction on ice.
Here friction slows the box.

solution: The shoe grips the ground. Friction on the shoe lets the person push off and walk forward.

questions.stem: A footballer kicks a ball that is rolling towards him. The ball goes in the opposite direction at a higher speed. Which effects does the kick have?
options: It changes the direction and speeds the ball up
It changes the direction and slows the ball down
It only speeds the ball up
It only changes the direction of the ball

explain.why: The ball goes faster than before, not slower.
The ball also goes in a new direction.
The ball also moves faster.

solution: Moving the opposite way means the direction changed.
A higher speed means it also sped up.

questions.stem: A girl stretches a spring with her hands. Then she lets it go and the spring pulls her hands back together. What does her force do to the spring and what makes it pull back?
options: It makes the spring speed up, and friction makes it pull back
It changes the shape of the spring, and elastic spring force makes it pull back
It makes the spring move, and magnetic force makes it pull back
It changes the shape of the spring, and gravity makes it pull back

explain.why: Friction acts when surfaces rub. It is not what pulls the spring back.
The spring is not a magnet. The pull back is elastic spring force.
Gravity pulls down. The pull back is the spring's own force.

solution: Stretching changes the spring's shape.
A stretched spring pulls back by elastic spring force.

questions.stem: A bird sits on a wire. The wire sags a little but does not break and goes back to its shape when the bird leaves. Which statement is correct?
options: Friction pulls the wire down and gravity pushes the bird up
Magnetic force holds the bird on the wire
Gravity pulls the bird down and the sagging wire pushes back with an elastic force
Gravity pulls the wire up and the bird pushes down with friction

explain.why: Gravity pulls down, not up.
Birds are not attracted by magnets.
Gravity pulls things down, and friction does not hold the bird up.

solution: The bird is pulled down by gravity.
The wire changes shape and pushes back like a spring.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes what happens when a car driver presses the brake pedal harder and harder as the car comes to a stop?
options: The magnetic force is greater and the car stops at once
The force of friction on the wheels is smaller and the car speeds up
The force of gravity is greater and the car speeds up
Friction on the wheels is greater and the car slows more

explain.why: Brakes use friction, not magnetic force.
Brakes are used to slow the car, with more friction.
Gravity does not change when the brake is pressed.

solution: Pressing harder makes friction bigger, so the car slows faster.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an example of a force acting without contact?
options: A wind pushing against a flag
A magnet attracting an iron nail from a short distance
The Earth pulling an apple towards the ground

explain.why: Gravity acts across space.
A magnet pulls without touching, so this is a non-contact force.
Gravity pulls without touching.

solution: Wind has to touch the flag to push it. The other three forces act across a gap.

questions.stem: A cricketer catches a fast ball with a pair of soft gloves and pulls his hands back as he catches. Which effects does the force of his hands have on the ball?
options: The ball keeps going at the same speed
The ball changes direction and keeps moving
The ball slows down and stops
The ball speeds up and goes in a new direction

explain.why: A force on the ball changes its motion.
The ball stops in his hands.
A catch does not speed up the ball.

solution: Force from his hands slows the ball until it stops in his hands.

questions.stem: A boy pulls a stretched elastic band and lets go. A small ball placed against the band shoots out. What does the force from the band do to the ball?
options: It changes the shape of the ball for ever
It makes the ball start to move and speeds it up
It makes the ball stop moving
It makes the ball slow down

explain.why: The ball keeps its shape. It moves.
The ball was still, and then it shoots away.
The ball moves faster, not slower.

solution: The stretched band pushes the ball, so the ball goes from still to moving fast.

questions.stem: Two students argue about a book on a table. Aini says: 'Gravity is pulling the book down.' Dev says: 'No force is acting on it because it is not moving.' Who is correct, and why?
options: Aini, because gravity pulls on the book all the time
Dev, because the table cancels gravity
Dev, because forces only act on moving objects
Both are correct since forces come and go

explain.why: The table does not remove gravity. The book is still pulled down.
Forces act on still objects too.
Gravity does not come and go. Dev is wrong.

solution: Gravity pulls on every object near the Earth all the time, even if it is still.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct pair of a force and an example?
options: Elastic spring force: a trampoline pushing a jumper up
Gravitational force: a fridge magnet holding a note
Frictional force: a bar magnet lifting a pin
Magnetic force: a stone falling off a cliff

explain.why: A fridge magnet holds the note by magnetic force.
A magnet lifts a pin by magnetic force.
A falling stone is pulled by gravity.

solution: A trampoline stretches and then pushes back with an elastic spring force.

questions.stem: A paper clip is dropped from a table, and it falls. A student holds a magnet above it, and the clip is pulled up and sticks to the magnet. Which statement explains this?
options: The magnetic force on the clip is greater than the gravity on it
Friction between the magnet and clip lifts the clip
The magnetic force on the clip is smaller than the gravity on it
Gravity stops acting on the clip near a magnet

explain.why: Friction does not lift the clip. The magnet does.
If it were smaller, the clip would not move up.
Gravity always acts on the clip.

solution: The clip moves up, so the upward magnetic force is greater than the downward gravity.

questions.stem: A bowling ball hits a pin. The pin flies away and the ball slows down. What do the forces between them do?
options: They change the motion of the ball only
They change the motion of the pin only
They change the motion of both objects
They change the shape of the pin only

explain.why: The pin moves as well.
The ball slows down as well.
The question is about motion, and both objects change motion.

solution: Forces act on both objects when they hit.
The pin goes from still to moving and the ball slows down.

questions.stem: A student hangs a ball on a spring from a stand. The spring stretches and then the ball stays still. Which forces act on the ball?
options: Elastic spring force down and gravity up
Magnetic force down and gravity up
Gravity down and elastic spring force up

explain.why: Gravity pulls down and the spring pulls up.
There is no magnet. Gravity pulls down.
There is nothing rubbing against the ball.

solution: Gravity pulls the ball down.
The stretched spring pulls it up.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of gravitational force?
options: It makes moving objects speed up all the time
It pulls everything on Earth towards the ground
It only acts when objects touch
It only pulls on things made of iron

explain.why: Gravity can also slow things, such as a ball thrown up.
Gravity acts without touching.
That describes magnetic force.

solution: Gravity pulls everything towards the Earth, with or without contact.

questions.stem: Zara pulls a toy wagon along the floor with a string. Which describes the force from the string on the wagon?

explain.why: A string cannot push. It pulls the wagon.
A pull moves the wagon towards the person pulling.
A push moves an object away from the one who pushes.

solution: The string pulls the wagon towards Zara.

questions.stem: A stone sits still on the ground. Which force is acting on it?
options: No force, since the stone is still

explain.why: No spring is stretched or squashed.
Gravity pulls on the stone all the time, even when it is still.
A stone is not attracted by a magnet.

solution: Gravity always pulls the stone towards the Earth.

questions.stem:
Which of the following show a force making a still object start to move?
A: A girl kicks a ball lying on the grass.
B: A man stops a rolling ball with his foot.
C: A boy pulls a wagon that is standing still.
D: A cook flattens a ball of dough.

explain.why: D changes the shape of dough. It does not make it move.
B shows a force stopping a moving ball.
B stops a ball and D changes a shape.

solution: A and C: a force makes a still ball and a still wagon move.
B stops a moving ball. D changes shape.

questions.stem: A ball is dropped and hits the floor. It squashes slightly and bounces up. Which effects of a force are shown?
options: Change of shape and change of direction

explain.why: The ball also goes up instead of down, so its direction changes too.
The ball is also squashed for a moment.
The ball squashes and goes the other way, so both change.

solution: The floor squashes the ball for a moment (shape).
Then the ball moves up instead of down (direction).

questions.stem: A girl pulls a cart that is standing still. What does her force do to the cart?
options: It makes the cart start to move
It makes the cart stay still
It changes the shape of the cart for ever

explain.why: A pull large enough to move the cart gets it going.
A force does not change how heavy the cart is.
The cart does not change shape. It moves.

solution: A pull makes a still object start to move.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about forces is correct?
options: Friction acts even when the surfaces do not touch
Gravity pulls only on things that are falling
A spring has a force only when it is pushed
A magnet can pull a paper clip without touching it

explain.why: Friction needs the surfaces to touch.
Gravity pulls on all things all the time, even those that are still.
A spring also has force when pulled or stretched.

solution: A magnetic force acts through a gap, so a magnet can pull a paper clip from a distance.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of an object and the force acting on it is NOT correct?
options: A ball falling from a roof: gravity pulls it down
An iron nail on a table: elastic spring force pulls it down
A sled slowing down on snow: friction
A paper clip near a magnet: magnetic force

explain.why: This pair is correct.
This pair is correct.
This pair is correct.

solution: The pull on a nail on a table is gravity, not elastic spring force. The other pairs are correct.

questions.stem:
Which of the following can a force do to an object?
A: Make a still object move.
B: Make a moving object stop.
C: Make an object lighter.
D: Make an object change direction.

explain.why: C is wrong. A force does not change how heavy an object is.
C is wrong, and it leaves out B, which is correct.
C is wrong, and it leaves out A, which is correct.

solution: A, B and D are effects of a force.
A force cannot make an object lighter.

questions.stem:
Zhen pushes a sled on a flat field of snow and lets go. The sled slows down and stops. Which statements are correct?
A: The sled slows down because of friction.
B: A force is needed to stop the sled.
C: The sled stops because there is no force on it.
D: Friction makes the sled move faster.

explain.why: Both are wrong. Friction acts on the sled and slows it.
D is wrong. Friction slows the sled down.
C is wrong. A force (friction) is acting on the sled.

solution: Friction slows the sled and stops it.
Stopping a moving object needs a force, and friction supplies it.

questions.stem: A diving board bends down when a girl stands at its end and goes back to its shape after she leaves. Which statement is correct?
options: Gravity pulls the girl down and the bent board pushes up with elastic spring force
Magnetic force pulls the girl down and the bent board pushes with friction
Gravity pushes the board up and the girl pulls it down with friction
The board stays bent because no force acts on it

explain.why: The girl is not pulled down by a magnet, and friction is not what pushes the board back up.
Gravity pulls down, not up.
The board goes back to its shape because of its own elastic force.

solution: Gravity pulls the girl down and bends the board.
The bent board pushes up with elastic spring force.

questions.stem: A heavy book is placed on a coil spring and squashes it. The book stays still. Which statement is correct?
options: The squashed spring pulls the book down with elastic spring force
The spring pushes the book up with magnetic force
The spring pushes the book up with gravity
The squashed spring pushes the book up with elastic spring force

explain.why: A squashed spring pushes out, so it pushes the book up.
The spring is not a magnet.
Gravity pulls the book down, not up.

solution: A squashed spring pushes back. It holds up the book.
This is elastic spring force.

questions.stem: Which statement about forces is correct?
options: Gravitational force: needs the objects to touch
Elastic spring force: acts only on magnets

explain.why: Gravity pulls from a distance.
It acts on any stretched or squashed spring or rubber band.
Friction needs the two surfaces to touch.

solution: Magnetic force can act across a gap, so that statement is true. The others are not.

questions.stem: A ball thrown upwards slows down, stops for a moment and falls. Which force mainly slows it going up?
options: The push from the thrower's hand

explain.why: There is no spring.
The hand's push ends when the ball leaves it. It cannot slow the ball.
There is no magnet.

solution: Gravity pulls down on the ball all the time, so it slows going up and speeds up coming down.

questions.stem: A parked car is pushed to the right by a man but it does not move. Which of the following is the best explanation?
options: The man's push has no effect on a heavy car like this
The push is not big enough to overcome the friction at the tyres
Gravity holds the car off the ground
The car has no weight so it cannot move

explain.why: A push is a force, and it would move a car if it were big enough.
Gravity pulls the car down towards the ground.
The car has weight. It does not move because of friction.

solution: The friction at the tyres balances the push. The push is not big enough to overcome the friction, so the car stays still.

questions.stem: A wooden block is pulled to the right by a spring and slides across a rough table. Arrows P, Q and R show forces on the block. Which arrow shows the frictional force?

explain.why: A block sliding on a rough table has friction, shown by one of the arrows.
Arrow P points the way the block is pulled. Friction acts against the motion.
Arrow R points down, towards the ground. That is the pull of gravity.

solution: Friction acts opposite to the motion of the block, so it points left (arrow Q).

questions.stem: A wooden block is pulled to the right by a spring and slides across a rough table. Arrows P, Q and R show forces on the block. Which arrow shows the gravitational force?

explain.why: Arrow P points the way the block is pulled by the spring.
Both of those arrows point sideways. Gravity points down.
Arrow Q points opposite to the motion. That is friction.

solution: Gravity pulls things towards the Earth, so it is the arrow pointing down (R).

questions.stem: A wooden block is pulled to the right by a spring and slides across a rough table. Arrows P, Q and R show forces on the block. Which arrow shows the elastic spring force?

explain.why: Arrow R points down. That is gravity.
Neither of these is the pull of the spring.
Arrow Q points the opposite way to the spring's pull. That is friction.

solution: The stretched spring pulls the block towards itself, to the right (arrow P).

explain.why: Arrow A shows the girl's pull on the spring, to the right.
Arrow D points up, and no force acts that way here.
Arrow C points down. That is gravity.

solution: The stretched spring pulls back towards the wall, to the left (B).

questions.stem: An iron ball hangs in the air below a magnet and does not touch it. Arrows X and Y act on the ball. Which statement is correct?
options: X is the gravitational force and Y is the magnetic force
X is the magnetic force and Y is the elastic spring force
X is the frictional force and Y is the gravitational force
X is the magnetic force and Y is the gravitational force

explain.why: Gravity pulls down (Y). The magnet pulls the iron ball up (X).
There is no spring. The downward force is gravity.
The ball is not touching anything, so there is no friction.

solution: The magnet pulls the iron ball up (X, magnetic force).
The Earth pulls it down (Y, gravity).

explain.why: Only one arrow points the way he pushes.
Arrow P points back towards the boy, opposite to his push. It is friction.
The push is one of the arrows.

solution: The boy is on the left and pushes the box away from him, to the right. That is arrow Q.

questions.stem: A toy car is rolled across four floors. On which floor will it stop the soonest?

explain.why: A smooth surface has little friction, so the car goes further.
Ice has very little friction, so the car goes a long way.
A polished surface is smooth, so the car goes further than on carpet.

solution: A rough surface has more friction, so the car loses speed and stops sooner.

questions.stem: A box is sliding to the right across a floor. In which direction does friction act on the box?
options: To the right, the same way as the motion
To the left, against the motion

explain.why: Friction does not help the box slide. It acts against the motion.
Friction acts along the surface, not upwards.
Gravity acts downwards. Friction acts along the surface against the motion.

solution: Friction always acts opposite to the way an object moves or tries to move.

questions.stem: Why do running shoes have grooves on their soles?
options: To make the shoes lighter in the air
To reduce friction so the runner can slide
To make the shoes look nicer
To give more grip on the ground

explain.why: Grooves are for grip, not for lightness.
Grooves grip the ground. They increase friction.
The grooves have a job: they stop slipping.

solution: Grooves grip the ground. More friction means the shoe does not slip.

questions.stem: Why is oil put on the chain of a bicycle?
options: To make the chain stick to the wheel
To reduce friction between the metal parts
To increase friction between the metal parts

explain.why: Oil makes parts slide past each other more easily.
Oil does not make the chain heavy.
Oil makes surfaces slippery, so there is less friction.

solution: Oil makes the surfaces slippery. Friction goes down and the chain moves more easily.

questions.stem: Mei pushes a box along a smooth floor, then along a rough carpet with the same push. On which surface does the box move the shorter distance after she lets go?
options: It moves the same distance on both
It does not move on either surface

explain.why: A smooth floor has less friction, so the box goes further.
The two surfaces have different amounts of friction.
The push makes the box move on both surfaces.

solution: More friction on the carpet makes the box stop sooner.

questions.stem: Which of the following ways will reduce the friction when moving a heavy box?

explain.why: A rougher floor means more friction.
Rubber grips the floor, so there is more friction.
Sand makes the floor rougher, so there is more friction.

solution: Wheels roll instead of rubbing, so there is much less friction.

questions.stem: Which of these activities needs friction?
options: Walking on a path without slipping
Pushing a toy car on a smooth table

explain.why: Skating needs little friction.
A car moves further when there is little friction.
A slide works best with little friction.

solution: Friction between the shoe and the ground stops us from slipping when we walk.

questions.stem: A pencil eraser gets smaller as it rubs against paper. Which force makes the eraser wear away?

explain.why: Gravity pulls the eraser down. Rubbing causes the wear.
An eraser is not a magnet.
There is no spring involved.

solution: Rubbing against paper causes friction, which wears the eraser away.

questions.stem: A spring is hung from a stand. Gina replaces a 100 g mass by a 200 g mass. What happens to the spring?
options: It becomes shorter and then longer

explain.why: A bigger mass pulls harder, so the spring stretches more.
The spring only stretches more when the load is bigger.
A greater load stretches a spring more.

solution: A bigger load pulls the spring more, so it is longer.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to measure the size of a force?

explain.why: A measuring cylinder measures volume.
A stopwatch measures time.
A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.stem: A 50 g mass stretches a spring by 2 cm. The same spring is stretched by a 175 g mass. If the stretch is in proportion to the load, how much will it stretch?

explain.why: 6 cm is the stretch with 150 g.
50 g gives 2 cm, so 175 g gives 3.5 times as much: 7 cm.
8 cm is the stretch with 200 g.

solution: 175 g is 3.5 times 50 g, so the stretch is 3.5 x 2 = 7 cm.

questions.stem: A bag hangs from a spring balance and the reading is 6 N. What does the reading tell us?
options: The bag has a mass of 6 N
Friction on the bag is 6 N
The Earth pulls the bag down with 6 N
The spring pushes the bag down with 6 N

explain.why: Mass is not measured in newtons.
Nothing is rubbing against the bag.
The spring pulls up. The bag's weight pulls down.

solution: The reading shows the weight of the bag, which is the pull of gravity on it.

questions.stem: Ali pushes a book along a table and it stops as soon as he lets go. When he puts a few pencils under the book, it slides further. Why?
options: The pencils roll, so friction is less
The pencils make the book heavier on the table
The pencils push the book forward

explain.why: Rolling pencils reduce friction.
Pencils do not make the book heavier. They reduce friction.
Pencils do not push. They roll.

solution: Rolling has much less friction than sliding. So the book goes further.

questions.stem: Two identical springs P and Q hang with different loads. P has a 100 g mass and Q has a 50 g mass. Which statement is correct?
options: P is longer than Q because it has the bigger load
Q is longer than P because it has the smaller load
P and Q are the same length
P is shorter than Q because it is heavier

explain.why: The bigger load stretches a spring more.
The loads are different.
A heavier load makes the spring longer, not shorter.

solution: The spring with the bigger load stretches more, so P is longer.

questions.stem: Siti rolls a car down a ramp onto four surfaces. The table shows how far it travelled. Which conclusion is supported?
options: The car travelled furthest on the plastic sheet, so that has the least friction
Tiles have more friction than the rubber mat
The heavier the surface, the further the car travels
The car travels furthest on the surface with the most friction

explain.why: The car went further on tiles (85 cm) than on the rubber mat (25 cm), so tiles have less friction.
The weight of the surface was not tested.
More friction makes the car go a shorter distance.

solution: Plastic sheet: 110 cm, the furthest. So it has the least friction.
Rubber mat has the most friction.

questions.stem: The table shows the length of a spring for different loads. The spring is 24 cm long with an unknown load. What is the load?

explain.why: 300 g would make the spring 22 cm long.
250 g would make the spring 20 cm long.
400 g would make the spring 26 cm long.

solution: Each 50 g adds 2 cm. From 10 cm to 24 cm is 14 cm.

questions.stem: A spring is 12 cm long with no load. A 100 g load makes it 16 cm and a 200 g load makes it 20 cm. What is its length with a 350 g load, if it keeps stretching in the same way?

explain.why: This is the length with 300 g.
The length is not 350 g divided by anything. Add the stretch (14 cm) to 12 cm.
This is the length with 250 g.

solution: The stretch is 4 cm for each 100 g.
350 g stretches it 14 cm, so the length is 12 + 14 = 26 cm.

questions.stem: A load was hung on a spring. When the load was removed, the spring did not go back to its first length. What is the most likely reason?
options: The spring was not hung from a stand
The spring was too short at the start
The spring was stretched too much
The spring was hung from a stand that was too low

explain.why: A stand has nothing to do with it.
A short spring is not damaged by length alone.
The height of the stand does not change how far the spring itself is stretched.

solution: A spring that is stretched too far is damaged and cannot go back to its first length.

questions.stem: On a wet road, a car takes a longer distance to stop than on a dry road. What is the best explanation?
options: The tyres become smooth when they are wet
Water between the tyres and the road reduces friction
Water increases friction between the tyres and the road
The wet road makes the car heavier

explain.why: The tyres stay the same. The water is on the road.
Water makes the road slippery. Friction decreases.
The weight of the car does not change.

solution: Water acts like oil. Less friction means the brakes stop the car less quickly.

questions.stem: A skater glides far across smooth ice after one push. A skater pushed once on a rough floor stops quickly. Which statement explains why?
options: Ice has more friction so the skater keeps moving
There is no friction on ice or on the rough floor
The rough floor has no friction
Ice has less friction so the skater loses speed slowly

explain.why: More friction would stop the skater faster.
Friction acts on both. It is just much smaller on ice.
Rough floors have a lot of friction.

solution: Less friction means the skater slows down slowly and goes far.

questions.stem: Mei pushes the same box with the same push once on a floor covered with sandpaper and once on a polished floor. Which statement is correct?
options: The box travels further on the smooth floor because there is less friction
The box travels further on the rough floor because the box is heavier there
The box travels the same distance because the push is the same
The box travels further on the rough floor because there is more friction

explain.why: The box weighs the same on both floors.
Different friction gives different distances.
More friction stops the box sooner.

solution: Less friction on the smooth floor means the box slows down more slowly and goes further.

questions.stem: A block is pulled across a table with a spring balance at a steady speed. The reading on cloth is 5 N. The same block is pulled on glass. What is the reading likely to be?

explain.why: Glass is smoother than cloth, so there is less friction.
The surfaces have different friction.
Some friction still acts on glass, so a small pull is needed.

solution: Glass has less friction than cloth, so a smaller pull is needed.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about friction are correct?
A: It makes moving objects slow down.
B: It produces heat when surfaces rub.
C: It is bigger on a smooth surface than a rough one.
D: It acts only when objects are moving.

explain.why: D is wrong. Friction can act on a still object that is being pushed.
C is wrong. A smooth surface has less friction.
Both are wrong.

solution: Friction slows moving objects and makes heat when surfaces rub.
It is smaller on smooth surfaces.

questions.stem: Three tests use a ramp and a toy car. The ramp heights and distances moved on carpet are: 10 cm, 30 cm; 20 cm, 55 cm; 30 cm, 80 cm. Which conclusion is correct?
options: The lower the ramp, the further the car moves
The height of the ramp has no effect
The car moves further on a rough surface
A higher ramp makes the car go further

explain.why: The 30 cm ramp gave the longest distance.
The distance changes with the height.
The surface was not changed in these tests.

solution: The distance goes up as the height goes up: 30, 55, 80 cm.

questions.stem: Ali's results for a ramp experiment do not show a clear pattern. He used a different toy car for each surface. What should he do to make his test fair?
options: Use a different ramp for each surface
Release the cars from different heights
Use the same toy car for every surface

explain.why: This would add another variable.
One measurement is not reliable. Repeating helps.
The height should be the same for every surface.

solution: Only the surface should change. The car, ramp and height must stay the same.

questions.stem: Mei compares two different springs P and Q to see which stretches more. What must she keep the same for both springs?
options: The number of coils in the springs

explain.why: These may be the difference being tested.
The springs are different, and that is what she is comparing.
Colour does not affect stretching.

solution: To compare the springs, the load and first length should be the same.

questions.stem: A heavy box is pushed along the floor. Which action will make the box stop sooner after a push?
options: Placing a rough mat under it

explain.why: Rollers reduce friction, so the box slides further.
Oil reduces friction.
Polished tiles have less friction than carpet.

solution: A rough mat increases friction, so the box stops sooner.

questions.stem: Why do machines have oil between their moving metal parts?
options: It increases friction so that the parts stay in place
It reduces friction and wear on the parts

explain.why: Oil reduces friction.
Oil has no effect on magnetism.
The oil is a thin layer. It is not for weight.

solution: Oil keeps the metal parts from rubbing directly, so less friction, less heat and less wear.

questions.stem: A block hangs from a spring balance and does not move. Which two forces act on the block?
options: Its weight down and the spring force up
Its weight downwards and friction upwards
Magnetic force downwards and the spring force upwards
Its weight upwards and the spring force downwards

explain.why: There is no rubbing surface, so no friction.
A magnet is not involved. Gravity pulls down.
Weight acts down.

solution: Gravity pulls the block down.
The stretched spring pulls it up with the same size of force, so it stays still.

questions.stem: The graph shows how the length of a spring changes with load. What is the first length of the spring, with no load?

explain.why: A spring has length even with no load.
12 cm is the length with 100 g.
2 cm is the stretch for 50 g, not the first length.

solution: With no load (0 g), the line starts at 8 cm.

14 cm is the length with 150 g. The spring gains 2 cm per 50 g.
The spring gains 2 cm per 50 g, so only 16 cm.

solution: The length goes up by 2 cm for each 50 g.
At 150 g it is 14 cm, so at 200 g it is 16 cm.

questions.stem: Two bags hang from separate spring balances. Bag X reads 8 N and bag Y reads 3 N. Which statement is correct?
options: X has less matter than Y
The Earth pulls X with a bigger force than Y
The Earth pulls X and Y with the same force
Y is pulled by the Earth with a bigger force than X

explain.why: The bigger weight means more matter, not less.
The readings are different.
The bigger reading means the bigger pull.

solution: The reading is the weight. The bigger reading (8 N) is the bigger pull of the Earth.

questions.stem: A spring balance has a spring that stretches more for a heavier load. Why must the scale on a spring balance have equal spaces between marks?
options: The spring does not stretch at all
A spring stretches equally for each equal extra load
The spring stretches more and more for each extra gram
The marks are only there to make the scale look neat

explain.why: A spring balance works because the spring stretches.
A spring stretches by equal amounts for equal extra loads.
The spaces show forces. They are equal because of how the spring stretches.

solution: A spring stretches in equal steps for equal extra loads, so the scale can be marked evenly.

questions.stem: Which action makes it harder to slide a heavy cupboard across the floor?
options: Putting a wet cloth under the cupboard
Putting small wheels on the cupboard
Putting a rubber mat under it

explain.why: Wetness reduces friction.
Wheels reduce friction.
Oil makes it easier to slide.

solution: A rubber sheet grips the floor, so friction is greater.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about the weight of an object are correct?
A: It is the pull of the Earth on the object.
B: It is measured in newtons.
C: It is the same as the amount of matter in the object.
D: It acts upwards.

explain.why: Both C and D are wrong. Weight is a force that acts downwards.
Weight acts downwards, towards the Earth, so D is wrong.
Weight is a force. It is not the amount of matter, so C is wrong.

solution: A and B are correct: weight is the Earth's pull on an object and is measured in newtons.
Weight is a force, not an amount of matter, and it acts downwards.

questions.stem: The table shows the length of two springs, P and Q, with different loads. Which statement is correct?
options: Springs P and Q stretch by the same amount for the same load
Spring Q stretches more than spring P for the same load
Spring P stretches more than spring Q for the same load
Spring Q is longer than spring P with no load

explain.why: The lengths of the two springs do not change by the same amount.
Spring P gains 2 cm for each 50 g and spring Q gains 4 cm, so Q stretches more.
Both springs are 10 cm long with no load.

solution: From 0 g to 100 g, spring P grows from 10 cm to 14 cm and spring Q from 10 cm to 18 cm.

questions.stem: A cyclist squeezes the brakes and the bicycle slows down. The brake pads become warm. Which statement explains why?
options: The magnetic force of the wheel produces heat
The pull of gravity on the pads produces heat
Friction between pads and wheel makes heat
The elastic spring force in the brake produces heat

explain.why: A bicycle wheel does not act as a magnet on the pads.
Gravity does not rub the pads against the wheel.
The spring only pulls the pads back. It does not rub against the wheel.

solution: The pads rub against the moving wheel. Friction slows the wheel and makes the pads warm.

questions.stem: A block is pulled at a steady speed along a table by a spring balance that reads 4 N. What is the size of the friction between the block and the table?

explain.why: The friction is not twice the pull. A steady speed means the two are equal.
Friction acts on any block sliding on a table. Here it is as big as the pull.
The friction is not half the pull. A steady speed means the two are equal.

solution: The block moves at a steady speed, so the friction is as big as the pull on the spring balance, 4 N.

questions.stem: Zhi Wei wants to find out whether a heavier block has more friction with a table. He pulls blocks of different weights with a spring balance. Which should he keep the same?
options: The reading on the spring balance
The material of the blocks and table
The weight of each block that he pulls
The number of blocks pulled at one time

explain.why: The reading is what he measures, so it can change.
The weight is the variable he is testing, so it must be different.
More blocks would make a heavier load, which changes the variable being tested.

solution: Only the weight should change. The block material and the table surface must stay the same so that the test is fair.
